subject: botany
question_text: Which are the three cells found in a pollen grain when it is shed at the three-celled stage?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section (book p.17, VSAQ 1). Botany holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The book prints 'at the three called stage' (scan error for 'three-celled stage'); the question text is cleaned.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants · 2 marks

steps.label: The three cells

lines.text: One vegetative cell and two male gametes.

steps.why: At the three-celled stage the generative cell has already divided, so the grain carries the vegetative cell plus the two male gametes it produced — that is the full count of three.
common_mistakes: Listing the generative cell as one of the three. At this stage it no longer exists — it has divided.
Writing 'two vegetative cells and one male gamete' — the counts reversed.
steps.memory_tip: Three-celled = 1 + 2: one vegetative cell, two male gametes.
steps.margin_note: One boxed line with the exact count earns this mark.

steps.label: Origin of the male gametes
lines: The two male gametes are formed when the
steps.why: The question hides a second point: where the two extra cells came from. Naming the generative cell's mitotic division shows you know the 2-celled to 3-celled change.
common_mistakes: Writing meiosis instead of mitosis. Meiosis made the microspore; inside the pollen grain every division is mitosis.
Saying the vegetative cell divides — it does not; it makes the pollen tube.
steps.memory_tip: Generative cell → (mitosis) → 2 male gametes. Meiosis happened earlier, in the microspore mother cell.
steps.margin_note: One sentence naming the generative cell and mitosis completes the answer.

insider_note: The mark-losing answer here is 'vegetative cell, generative cell, male gamete' — at the three-celled stage the generative cell has already divided, so it is not one of the three.
